intro: Field Trip Health Ottawa offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy as an outpatient service. The clinic recently left its downtown suite on Sparks Street and now works from Unit 402 at 1 Centrepointe Drive in Nepean, a medical office building near Baseline Road and Woodroffe Avenue.

It treats adults with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain and substance use problems, mostly people for whom medication and counselling have not done enough. Appointments run on weekdays and you go home the same day. Staff speak mainly English, but services are also offered in French, which helps clients coming from Gatineau, Orleans, Rockland and Embrun.

pillars.title: How a dosing session runs in Ottawa
pillars.body: Set aside about two and a half hours. You lie back in a zero-gravity chair with a weighted blanket, put on noise-cancelling headphones, and a nurse gives a low dose of ketamine, usually by injection. A therapist stays in the room throughout and spends time with you afterwards before you leave. Because of drowsiness, the clinic asks you not to drive home after a session, even if you parked on site.

pillars.title: A move from downtown to Centrepointe
pillars.body: The clinic used to be at 350 Sparks Street, a short walk from Parliament Hill. Its page now gives a new address at 1 Centrepointe Drive, Unit 402, in the Centrepointe area of Nepean, close to Baseline Road and Woodroffe Avenue. Parking is available at the building for a fee. Some older listings and directions online still show the Sparks Street suite, so double-check the address when you book.

pillars.title: Psychotherapists, nurses and a program coordinator
pillars.body: The Ottawa therapy team names Jason Taylor and Amanda Laprade, both registered psychotherapists. Elizabeth Beauchamp coordinates the clinic program, and nurse practitioners including Chelsea Griswold carry out the medical consultations, with Dr. Mario Nucci as the physician for Field Trip's Ontario clinics. The clinic says its therapists can work in English and French.

overviewH2: How care is organised at the Ottawa clinic
overview: A free 15-minute discovery call comes first. After that you complete a questionnaire and see a nurse practitioner for a 50-minute medical consultation, which OHIP does not pay for. This is the gatekeeping step. The nurse practitioner looks at your health history and medications and may rule the treatment out for reasons such as pregnancy, a history of psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension or a recent serious head injury.

The standard plans have 6 or 9 dosing sessions, each about two and a half hours long. A nurse gives the medicine, usually as an intramuscular injection, and a therapist is with you from start to finish. You then meet that therapist for integration, where you work through the session and connect it to what you came in for.

One of them, Jason Taylor, is a doctoral-level psychotherapist who works mainly with depression, anxiety and OCD, and another, Amanda Laprade, specialises in substance use. The clinic also offers individual therapy and pain management, and lists neurofeedback as coming soon. It does not do MDMA or psilocybin therapy. location.heading: Field Trip Health Ottawa in Ottawa, Ontario
location.intro: The clinic is now in Nepean, on Centrepointe Drive near Baseline Road and Woodroffe Avenue, after moving out of downtown Ottawa. Barrhaven and Kanata are about 15 to 20 minutes away by car, Orleans and Gatineau around 25 to 30, Brockville and Cornwall about an hour or a little more, and Toronto roughly four and a half hours on Highways 416 and 401.

faqIntro: Answers come from the Ottawa clinic's page on fieldtriphealth.ca. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Where is Field Trip Health Ottawa now?
faqs.a: The clinic has moved to 1 Centrepointe Drive, Unit 402, in the Centrepointe area of Nepean, Ottawa (K2G 6E2). It used to be at 350 Sparks Street downtown, and some directories and older directions still show that address. Parking at the new building costs extra, and you will need someone to drive you home after a dosing session.

faqs.q: Is Field Trip Health Ottawa a residential treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. It is a weekday outpatient clinic, and you leave after each appointment. It has no beds and does not offer detox. People who need a live-in addiction program or withdrawal management should ask the team for other options or compare residential centres in Ottawa and Eastern Ontario.

faqs.q: Can I get treatment in French?
faqs.a: Yes. Staff at the Ottawa clinic mainly speak English, but the clinic says it also offers services in French and that its therapists are fluent in both languages. Mention your preference on the discovery call.

faqs.q: What conditions does the Ottawa clinic treat?
faqs.a: Field Trip Health Ottawa uses ketamine-assisted psychotherapy mainly for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction and chronic pain. Its psychotherapists also work with grief, ADHD, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, complex PTSD and relationship concerns. The clinic describes the treatment as one possible option after other approaches, not a guaranteed fix.

faqs.q: How much does it cost, and does insurance help?
faqs.a: The clinic does not publish its fees; the cost depends on how many sessions you have and how the medicine is given, and the team explains it on a free discovery call. The 50-minute nurse practitioner consult is not covered by OHIP. Psychotherapy or nursing benefits from an extended health plan often cover part of the cost, and third-party financing is available.

Each dosing session at the Ottawa clinic takes about 2.5 hours, including preparation, the medicine and integration support. Most plans have 6 or 9 dosing sessions, followed by a review of whether more care would help.

faqs.q: Who is eligible, and do I need a referral?
faqs.a: You do not need a referral to book the discovery call, though physicians and nurse practitioners can refer patients through Field Trip's referral form or Ocean eReferral. Eligibility is decided by a nurse practitioner. The treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, allergic to the medicine, have a history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension or a recent severe head injury.

faqs.q: How do I prepare for a session?
faqs.a: Avoid alcohol and recreational substances beforehand and eat a light meal rather than a heavy one. Arrange transport home, because you may feel drowsy and the clinic says you will not be able to drive.

faqs.q: Does the Ottawa clinic offer MDMA or psilocybin therapy?
faqs.a: No. Only one psychedelic medicine can currently be prescribed for therapy in Canada, and that is the one the clinic uses, mainly by intramuscular injection. MDMA and psilocybin remain controlled substances that are not approved for routine clinical use.

faqs.q: Who operates Field Trip Health Ottawa?
faqs.a: The Ottawa clinic is one of eight Canadian clinics run as Field Trip Health Canada. When the original Field Trip Health company restructured in 2023, the Canadian clinics were taken over by the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing, while the US clinics went to a separate company. Use fieldtriphealth.ca to book in Ottawa.
